title: I Let the Clean-Room Gown-Slot Policy Survive Three Shift Bids

parts.text: The clean room booked gown slots in a spreadsheet the first shift bid promised to honor. After bid two, the new lead hung in my Tuesday slot because "gowns are fluid." I was thirty-six, operator, holding a booking that still said my name. I photographed the sheet and the lead's locker. I did not move my kit. Fluid, I said, could gown in overflow two.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Bid three is next month and the lead's locker is still on my Tuesday.

social.video_title: Fluid sat in my booked Tuesday gown slot — Part 1/3
social.description: Spreadsheet honor, a lead's locker, kit unmoved. Bid three is coming. Would you have relocated the kit?

parts.text: Bid three brought a badge system that read the old spreadsheet if you exported CSV. I exported. My Tuesday badge-locked the gown slot. The lead badge-errored in front of the auditor. I was still thirty-six, still not fluid. The auditor asked who owned the CSV. I forwarded the first bid's honor email.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The auditor has the honor email and a badge error on video.

social.video_title: The CSV badge-locked the gown slot they took — Part 2/3
social.description: Bid three, a badge error, an honor email. The auditor is watching. Does fluid export?

parts.text: Quality said honor emails survive shift bids. The lead gowns in overflow. My Tuesday slot has a label that outlived three bid posters. I gown on time and do not move for fluid. Fluid, it turns out, is a locker with no badge. The spreadsheet is now the system of record, which is a phrase auditors use when they have been embarrassed on camera.

social.video_title: Honor emails outlived three bid posters — Part 3/3
social.description: Quality, overflow gowns, a label that survived posters. Was fluid ever a locker?
